the_distinction_that_matters.question: Is injection a method choice inside a paper about something else, or has the pipeline itself been published as the contribution?
the_distinction_that_matters.answer: BOTH sets are non-empty, and the second set is the larger one at strong venues.

set_A_injection_as_the_contribution.reading: Our architecture CAN be a paper's headline. IEEE TAP and IEEE TMTT both accepted a paper whose entire product is a reusable aspect-indexed signature table with the downstream use stated as motivation and never run.

set_B_injection_as_a_method_choice.reading: In this set the table is plumbing. Potter and Costa still say exactly what their table is; LAMBDA does not.

what_actually_made_set_A_publishable.finding: In no case is 'we made a table' the contribution. Each one carries a second thing.

rows.the_second_thing: COMPRESSION - 12,100 triangles reduced to 10 clusters, plus two validations
STANDARDISATION - adopted into 3GPP at RAN1 #120, plus a held-out band test
RESOLUTION - a measurement nobody else had at that radial and angular resolution
A BRIDGE - the regression that maps slow reflectivity onto fast scatterer positions, plus end-to-end hardware validation
COVERAGE - 4 airframes, 1.8-27 GHz, monostatic and bistatic to 90 deg
A RELEASED TOOL - a public generator implementing the standard
A MEASUREMENT CHECK on a computed sigma inside the channel equation

our_artefact_as_measured.arithmetic: 5 airframes x 3 bands x 9 elevations x 120 azimuths = 16,200
our_artefact_as_measured.file_hygiene_note: the file also carries x500v2 and typhoonh480 keys with full 9x120 grids, left over from an earlier run. meta.drones_merged names only the 5 above, so every published count must use 5.
our_artefact_as_measured.engine: SBR (rcs_sbr_batch, 1-bounce, penetrate=True), div=16, jitter=2, on Sionna's Mitsuba ray engine

conclusion_1_our_contribution_cannot_be_.statement: Injection is mainstream and standardised, so 'we make an aspect-by-frequency sigma table' is not a contribution. Set A shows every published table carried a second thing - compression, resolution, a bridge, coverage, a tool, or a validation.
conclusion_1_our_contribution_cannot_be_.consequence: Our claim has to name the second thing explicitly, and the honest candidates are (a) the density and transparency of the grid, and (b) that signature and propagation come from the SAME ray engine.

conclusion_2_validation_is_NOT_the_open_.statement: ⭐ RETRACT the working assumption that nobody validated their injected signature. Five peer-reviewed instances did, with methods stronger than ours in places.
who_validated_and_how: P2-ZHANG-JSAC: 0.5 m metal sphere (theory -7.07 vs measured -8.96 dBsm) AND a held-out 28 GHz band
P6-DEEP-IET: end-to-end against a 77 GHz automotive radar, NMSE < 10%, SSIM > 81%
P1-SCHULER-TAP: anechoic bistatic measurements at the EC JRC Ispra, then the reduced model back against the full ray-trace
P7-DAS-WCL: reference cylinder calibration plus Anderson-Darling goodness-of-fit
P9-ZHANG-DCN: a PO-computed sigma checked against measured channel power, 0.11 to 7 dB
P5-COSTA-JSTEAP: signature shape only, Pearson 0.98 on normalised signatures
conclusion_2_validation_is_NOT_the_open_.consequence: The differentiator is narrower than we assumed. What remains open is not 'did anyone validate' but a much smaller gap - see conclusion 3.

conclusion_3_the_actual_remaining_gap.statement: Nobody in the set found computes the signature IN a communications ray engine and then injects it into that same engine's propagation paths.
why_each_near_miss_misses: P6-DEEP-IET computes in its own SBR solver but consumes in a free-space FMCW signal model - no propagation channel
P1-SCHULER-TAP computes in its own ray solver and never runs the downstream consumer
P9-ZHANG-DCN computes with PO and consumes in a GBSM, not a ray tracer
X1-LAMBDA consumes in ray-traced Sionna RT paths but computes in a separate commercial solver, and it is a preprint
conclusion_3_the_actual_remaining_gap.scope_label: established over the search coverage in this file; NOT a claim about all literature

pec_sphere_check_PASS.reading: the kernel converges to analytic PO within 0.20 dB; the residual against exact Mie is the price of the PO approximation, not a numerical defect

calibration_sphere_PASS.sphere: Yuan's own 17.8 cm metallic standard, stated -10 dBsm
calibration_sphere_PASS.reading: absolute scale and frequency flatness of the kernel are fine

phantom3_band_slope_FAIL.reading: our sigma runs about 4.4 dB low at 1.843 GHz, closing to inside the published envelope by 5.21 GHz. Above 6 GHz our band slope sits inside the measured range. The deficit is a low-frequency effect, and 1.8-6 GHz is the band this project works in.

conclusion_4_our_own_anchoring_is_partly.the_bar_the_venues_set: P2 calibrated on a sphere and held out a band. P6 compared end-to-end against hardware. We have the sphere half and we do not yet have the held-out or the end-to-end half.

what_it_means_for_us.the_paragraph_for_our_reports: 표적 서명을 전파 시뮬레이터 밖에서 만들어 각도·주파수 표로 저장하고 시뮬레이션 경로에 곱하는 구조는 이 분야의 표준 구조다. IEEE TAP(Schuler 2008), IEEE TMTT(Abadpour 2022), IET Radar Sonar Navig.(Deep 2020), IEEE JSAC(Zhang 2026), IEEE TAES(Potter 2025)에 실려 있고, 3GPP TR 38.901 V19.4.0 7.9.2.1 절이 그 구조를 그대로 규격화했다 — sigma_RCS = sigma_M·sigma_D·sigma_S 를 각도 섹터로 조회해 7.9.4.1 절 Step 10 의 경로전력과 Step 15 의 표적채널에 곱한다. 우리 sigma 격자(5기체 x 3밴드 x 고도 9 x 방위 120 = 16,200 값, outputs/report13_sigma_grid.json)는 같은 구조이며, 표를 누가 만드는가에서만 갈린다. 우리는 Schuler·Deep 계열 — 자체 광선/SBR 솔버 — 이고, 규격이 접은 두 축을 편다: 각도는 6 섹터 대신 9x120 표본, 주파수는 단일값 대신 3 밴드. 검증은 두 갈래로 서 있다. 커널은 해석 PO 대비 0.20 dB, Yuan 의 17.8 cm 교정구 대비 정확 Mie 기준 0.85 dB 안에서 맞는다(outputs/sbr_kr_sweep.json, outputs/validate_measured_airframe.json). 절대 레벨은 5.21 GHz 에서 공개 실측 envelope 안에 들어가고 1.843 GHz 에서 4.43 dB 낮다. 6 GHz 위에서 우리 밴드 기울기 0.264 dB/GHz 는 실측 0.21~0.315 dB/GHz 범위 안이다.
what_it_means_for_us.what_the_paragraph_deliberately_does_not: It does not claim injection is novel, it does not claim we validated more than the others, and it does not claim the FR1 absolute level is right.

cost_comparison.reading: Our whole 16,200-cell grid costs 17 minutes on one shared GPU. Our closest peer-reviewed relative (Deep, IET RSN 2020) spent 8 minutes on 20 CPU cores for one 77 GHz result set. The cost gap is not between injection and in-engine computation - both asymptotic routes land in minutes. The gap is against full-wave: 'several hours' per MLFMM simulation.
cost_comparison.hypothesis_labelled_as_a_hypothesis: A dense table is unaffordable by the commercial full-wave route. At several hours per simulation, 16,200 cells is out of reach, which would explain why LAMBDA prints no axes, no angular step and no dBsm value for its CADFEKO table, and why the commercial-solver-into-a-ray-tracer combination has no venue record. THIS IS AN INFERENCE FROM TWO COST FIGURES, NOT SOMETHING ANY PAPER STATES.
cost_comparison.the_concession_already_on_record: outputs/runtime_benchmark.json answer.cost_structure: in OUR implementation the PO integral costs 16.2x the ray cast at production batch size, because the integral runs in host numpy. SagittaSBR's device-side PO kernel is 6.5% of ray-launch time on an A100. The cascade is cheap when the integral is a device kernel; ours is not one yet.
